title: Sudoku graded by technique
description: Generate a 9 x 9 Sudoku that needs pairs or locked candidates: singles alone get stuck, but singles, naked and hidden pairs and locked candidates solve it. Both conditions are about pencil marks: the techniques get stuck exactly when some set of marks closed under them leaves a cell empty. 'Singles get stuck' is such a set, guessed in the abstraction; 'the stronger techniques solve it' says that no such set exists, so the check looks for one, and its marks are the counterexample. There is no uniqueness check: a puzzle that sound deductions solve has one solution. The refinement asks for a clue the counterexample's marks do not have.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The size of the puzzle and the derived domains. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% A 9 x 9 Sudoku: every row, every column and each of the nine 3 x 3 boxes contains the
% values 1..9 once. An instance may print clues pre(R,C,V) and may fix the solved grid with
% solution(R,C,V) (Instances tab).
row(1..9). col(1..9). val(1..9).
box(R,C,(R-1)/3*3+(C-1)/3) :- row(R), col(C).
printed(R,C) :- pre(R,C,_).

fragments.name: sudoku
fragments.description: The rules of the puzzle for any grid; used by solver A (one grid) and solver C (two grids).
fragments.text:
% The rules of the puzzle, for every grid G that a solver declares with grid(G):
% cell(G,R,C,V) says that grid G has the value V in row R, column C.
1 { cell(G,R,C,V) : val(V) } 1 :- grid(G), row(R), col(C).
:- cell(G,R,C1,V), cell(G,R,C2,V), C1 < C2.
:- cell(G,R1,C,V), cell(G,R2,C,V), R1 < R2.
:- cell(G,R1,C1,V), cell(G,R2,C2,V), box(R1,C1,B), box(R2,C2,B), (R1,C1) < (R2,C2).
% Every grid respects the printed clues.
:- grid(G), pre(R,C,V), not cell(G,R,C,V).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): a solved grid and k of its cells as clues.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a solved grid s and k of its cells that are revealed as clues.
% The grid is the instance's solution/3 if it gives one (then the grounder fixes it, which
% makes every solve call cheaper), otherwise any grid.
fixed :- solution(_,_,_).
grid(s) :- not fixed.
cell(s,R,C,V) :- solution(R,C,V).
:- fixed, pre(R,C,V), not solution(R,C,V).
k { clue(R,C) : row(R), col(C), not printed(R,C) } k.
% given(R,C,V): the puzzle shows the value V in row R, column C.
given(R,C,V) :- clue(R,C), cell(s,R,C,V).
#show given/3.

fragments.name: notes
fragments.description: Pencil marks closed under the techniques that leave a cell empty; in solver A (stuck with singles) and solver C (a counterexample: stuck with all techniques).
fragments.text:
% Pencil marks: out(R,C,V) says that V is crossed out in cell R,C, known(R,C,V) that V is
% written there. The techniques of the other fragments get stuck on a puzzle exactly when
% SOME set of marks that is closed under them leaves a cell empty: the marks they reach are
% the smallest closed set, which lies inside every other one. Each technique below is a
% constraint "if the premise holds in the marks, so does the result".
{ out(R,C,V) } :- row(R), col(C), val(V).
{ known(R,C,V) } :- row(R), col(C), val(V).
filled(R,C) :- known(R,C,_).
empty(R,C) :- row(R), col(C), not filled(R,C).
:- not empty(_,_).

% The units: nine rows, nine columns and nine boxes.
unit(r(R),R,C) :- row(R), col(C).
unit(c(C),R,C) :- row(R), col(C).
unit(b(B),R,C) :- box(R,C,B).
other(U,R,C,R2,C2) :- unit(U,R,C), unit(U,R2,C2), (R,C) != (R2,C2).
peer(R,C,R2,C2) :- other(_,R,C,R2,C2).

% Clues are written; a written value crosses out the other values in its cell and the
% value in the other cells of its units.
:- given(R,C,V), not known(R,C,V).
:- pre(R,C,V), not known(R,C,V).
:- known(R,C,V), val(W), W != V, not out(R,C,W).
:- known(R,C,V), peer(R,C,R2,C2), not out(R2,C2,V).

fragments.name: singles
fragments.description: Naked and hidden singles, as constraints on the marks. In both solvers.
fragments.text:
% Naked single: every other value is crossed out in the cell.
:- row(R), col(C), val(V), out(R,C,W) : val(W), W != V; not known(R,C,V).
% Hidden single: V is crossed out in every other cell of a unit.
:- unit(U,R,C), val(V), out(R2,C2,V) : other(U,R,C,R2,C2); not known(R,C,V).

fragments.name: pairs
fragments.description: Naked and hidden pairs. Only in solver C.
fragments.text:
% Naked pair: two cells of a unit have only V1 and V2 left; cross them out in the rest.
only2(R,C,V1,V2) :- row(R), col(C), val(V1), val(V2), V1 < V2,
    out(R,C,W) : val(W), W != V1, W != V2.
:- unit(U,R,C), val(V1), val(V2), V1 < V2, V = (V1;V2), not out(R,C,V),
    2 #count { R2,C2 : other(U,R,C,R2,C2), only2(R2,C2,V1,V2) }.
% Hidden pair: V1 and V2 are crossed out in every cell of a unit but the same two cells;
% cross out every other value in those two cells.
except2(U,V,R1,C1,R2,C2) :- other(U,R1,C1,R2,C2), (R1,C1) < (R2,C2), val(V),
    out(R,C,V) : unit(U,R,C), (R,C) != (R1,C1), (R,C) != (R2,C2).
hidden2(R1,C1,R2,C2,V1,V2) :- except2(U,V1,R1,C1,R2,C2), except2(U,V2,R1,C1,R2,C2), V1 < V2.
keep2(R1,C1,V1,V2) :- hidden2(R1,C1,_,_,V1,V2).
keep2(R2,C2,V1,V2) :- hidden2(_,_,R2,C2,V1,V2).
:- keep2(R,C,V1,V2), val(W), W != V1, W != V2, not out(R,C,W).

fragments.name: locked
fragments.description: Locked candidates (pointing and claiming). Only in solver C.
fragments.text:
% Locked candidates. Pointing: within box B, V is crossed out outside row R (column C);
% cross V out in the rest of that row (column).
boxrow(B,R) :- box(R,_,B).
boxcol(B,C) :- box(_,C,B).
:- boxrow(B,R), val(V), col(C2), not box(R,C2,B), not out(R,C2,V),
    out(R3,C3,V) : box(R3,C3,B), R3 != R.
:- boxcol(B,C), val(V), row(R2), not box(R2,C,B), not out(R2,C,V),
    out(R3,C3,V) : box(R3,C3,B), C3 != C.
% Claiming: within row R (column C), V is crossed out outside box B; cross V out in the
% rest of that box.
:- boxrow(B,R), val(V), box(R2,C2,B), R2 != R, not out(R2,C2,V),
    out(R,C3,V) : col(C3), not box(R,C3,B).
:- boxcol(B,C), val(V), box(R2,C2,B), C2 != C, not out(R2,C2,V),
    out(R3,C,V) : row(R3), not box(R3,C,B).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the clues with their values. The solved grid stays private to solver A.
fragments.text: glue(given(R,C,V)) :- row(R), col(C), val(V), not printed(R,C).

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for marks closed under all techniques with a cell left empty (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: marks that are closed under singles, pairs and locked candidates and
% leave a cell empty (fragment notes). Then these techniques do not solve the puzzle. If
% no such marks exist, they solve it, and so its solution is unique.
#show empty/2.

% Every puzzle whose clues are all written in these marks leaves them closed and a cell
% empty. So a clue must appear that the marks do not have.
relevant(given(R,C,V)) :- row(R), col(C), val(V), not printed(R,C), not known(R,C,V).
% Write as much as possible: the clause then names fewer clues.
#heuristic known(R,C,V) : row(R), col(C), val(V). [1,true]

fragments.name: view
fragments.description: A domain view (Observatory tab): the scene part draws what stays, the frame part one step, as draw/1 marks.
fragments.text:
% The grid, boxes in alternating borders; printed clues shaded.
#program scene.
draw(layout(grid)).
draw(cell(R,C)) :- row(R), col(C).
draw(attr(cell(R,C), stroke, box)) :- box(R,C,B), B \ 2 == 0.
draw(attr(cell(R,C), label, V)) :- pre(R,C,V).
draw(attr(cell(R,C), fill, printed)) :- pre(R,C,_).

#program frame.
draw(attr(cell(R,C), label, V)) :- cand(given(R,C,V)).
draw(attr(cell(R,C), fill, clue)) :- cand(given(R,C,_)).
% A counterexample: the cells its marks leave empty.
draw(attr(cell(R,C), fill, empty)) :- cex(empty(R,C)).
draw(emph(cell(R,C))) :- cex(empty(R,C)).
draw(note("Marks closed under all techniques leave the ringed cells empty.")) :- kind(reject).
draw(note("The techniques solve the puzzle.")) :- kind(solution).
#show draw/1.

fragments.name: check_plain
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: marks that are closed under singles, pairs and locked candidates and
% leave a cell empty (fragment notes). Then these techniques do not solve the puzzle. If
% no such marks exist, they solve it, and so its solution is unique.
#show empty/2.

% Every puzzle whose clues are all written in these marks leaves them closed and a cell
% empty. So a clue must appear that the marks do not have.
relevant(given(R,C,V)) :- row(R), col(C), val(V), not printed(R,C), not known(R,C,V).
% Variant no-heuristic: no preference for writing values, so the clauses may name more
% clues.
fragments.description: The check without the heuristic on known/3, for the variant no-heuristic.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + sudoku + abstraction + notes + singles      options "--project"
solver C = shared + notes + singles + pairs + locked + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts: % No printed clues: a puzzle with k = 26 clues (about 15 s).

% The graded puzzle with its first clue erased: 3 single clues give the grade back
% (k = 1; counted by a Python solver over every cell and value).
pre(1,4,4).
pre(2,1,4). pre(2,2,5). pre(2,7,2). pre(2,9,6).
pre(3,5,2). pre(3,8,8).
pre(4,1,7). pre(4,2,2). pre(4,4,8). pre(4,7,9). pre(4,8,6).
pre(5,1,6). pre(5,8,1).
pre(6,1,3).
pre(7,2,4). pre(7,5,1). pre(7,6,3).
pre(8,2,8). pre(8,6,4). pre(8,7,7). pre(8,8,5).
pre(9,1,5). pre(9,3,6). pre(9,5,8).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + sudoku + abstraction + notes + singles      options "--enum-mode=record --project"
solver C = shared + notes + singles + pairs + locked + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

generators.name: erased
generators.description: A random solved 9 x 9 grid (a fixed grid with its values, rows within bands, columns within stacks, bands and stacks permuted) with m random cells erased; redrawn unless the erased cells have a second completion, so the printed clues pre/3 never fix the grid.
generators.text:
% erased: a random solved grid with m cells erased, redrawn until the clues left have two completions
base(R,C,((R-1)*3+(R-1)/3+C-1)\9+1) :- R = 1..9, C = 1..9.
rmap(R,(@perm(3, (R-1)/3+1, bands)-1)*3+@perm(3, (R-1)\3+1, rows, (R-1)/3)) :- R = 1..9.
cmap(C,(@perm(3, (C-1)/3+1, stacks)-1)*3+@perm(3, (C-1)\3+1, cols, (C-1)/3)) :- C = 1..9.
full(R2,C2,@perm(9, V, vals)) :- base(R,C,V), rmap(R,R2), cmap(C,C2).
erased(R,C) :- full(R,C,_), @subset(m, 81, (R-1)*9+C, cells) = 1.
pre(R,C,V) :- full(R,C,V), not erased(R,C).
1 { alt(R,C,V) : V = 1..9 } 1 :- erased(R,C).
alt(R,C,V) :- pre(R,C,V).
:- alt(R,C1,V), alt(R,C2,V), C1 < C2.
:- alt(R1,C,V), alt(R2,C,V), R1 < R2.
:- alt(R1,C1,V), alt(R2,C2,V), (R1-1)/3 = (R2-1)/3, (C1-1)/3 = (C2-1)/3, (R1,C1) < (R2,C2).
:- alt(R,C,V) : erased(R,C), full(R,C,V).
#show pre/3.
